question.leadin: Answer the following about German invasions during World War II.
question.text: Germany invaded this country and Denmark as part of Operation Weserubung. This country was home to German heavy water production and was led by Vidkun Quisling after its surrender.
question.clue: Another leader of this country served with Josef Terboven and was executed with Albert Hagelin after establishing a fascist government.

swap.text: This northern neighbor of Germany lies on the Jutland peninsula. It also controls Greenland.
swap.clue: This country was defeated in one war after its adversary marched over a frozen strait to surprise its forces.

question.leadin: This member of the House of Vasa defeated Count Tilly in his most famous victory, Breitenfeld.
question.text: Name this man who died at the Battle of Lutzen and was known as the "Lion of the North."
question.answerHtml: Gustavus Adolphus [or Gustav Adolf; Gustav II; Gustavus the Great; prompt on “Gustav” or “Gustavus”]
question.clue: This man allegedly claimed that "the Lord God is my armor" before fighting without protection and dying at the Battle of Lutzen.

swap.leadin: The author of the Prose Edda, Snorri Sturluson, was a law speaker of a parliament in this country.
swap.text: Name this country home to the Althing, so-named to trick people to move to Greenland.
swap.clue: The ruling chiefs of this country established the Althing in the early 900s, one of the oldest continuously meeting parliaments in the world.

question.leadin: This country formed a dual monarchy with Denmark after the collapse of the Kalmar Union in 1521.
question.text: Name this country whose kings include Harald Hardrada.
question.clue: Magnus VI implemented a new code of laws called the Landslov that was implemented by King Magnus VI in 1274.

swap.text: This Viking explorer probably used a knarr, a type of Norse cargo vessel similar to a longship, in his expeditions to Vinland. This explorer is believed to be the first European to travel to North America.
swap.answerHtml: Leif Erikson [or Leif Erikson or Leiv Eiriksson or Leif the Lucky]
swap.clue: This explorer earned the nickname "Lucky" after rescuing a shipwrecked crew.

question.leadin: This institution was formed when Margaret I of Denmark's great-nephew, Erik of Pomerania, was crowned on Trinity Sunday.
question.text: Name this Nordic union established to counter the influence of the Hanseatic League. Internal conflict in this polity occurred primarily between Danish and Swedish "protectors of the realm" such as Sten Sture the Elder.
question.clue: Members of the Sture family served as regents to this state, which was targeted by the Engelbrekt rising.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of paper money.
swap.text: This European country was the first to print paper money, doing so from its central bank during the reign of Carl Gustaf. That central bank was based out of this country's capital at Stockholm.
swap.clue: The nobleman Johann Patkul ("PAHT-kool") helped forge a secret alliance against this country, where the Hats and Caps factions dominated a brief parliamentarian era called the Age of Liberty.

question.leadin: It arose over the control of the Hanko naval base and was prosecuted by the coalition government of Risto Ryti.
question.text: Name this war which saw the use of the Mannerheim line in an attempt to repel a Soviet invasion.
question.clue: Those clashes at Taipale and Summa are not as well known as the Battle of Raate Road, where one side used a decisive ambush; that was part of the larger Battle of Suomussalmi.

swap.leadin: Identify these victims of brazen assassinations from European history.
swap.text: South Africa's most evil export, superspy Craig Williamson, may have been responsible for the 1986 shooting of this Swedish Prime Minister, an ardent opponent of Apartheid.
swap.clue: This person succeeded his mentor, the country's longest serving PM, as party leader in 1969.

question.leadin: Christer Pettersen was convicted but later acquitted of this man's murder.
question.text: Name this politician from the Social Democratic Party, a prime minister of Sweden who was killed in 1986 while walking home from the cinema with his wife.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about everyone's favorite guild confederation, the Hanseatic League.
swap.text: The Hanseatic League became embroiled in the raids of the Victual Brothers, privateers hired by Albert of Mecklenburg to attack the ships of Margaret I, a queen of this country.
swap.clue: It's not Norway, but English kings Harold Harefoot and Harthacanute were from this country.

question.text: Cnut also overthrew St. Olaf of Norway; however, the Norwegian crown would soon pass to this illegitimate son of Olaf, who also became king of Denmark before dying at age 23.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of the good old-fashioned fun of throwing sticks.
swap.text: The stick throwing game of skittles originated in a region this country shares with its eastern neighbour. A bat sport invented by a veteran of this country's Civil War was demonstrated when it hosted the 1952 Summer Olympics.
swap.clue: Activists from this country's largest Germanic minority group cited scientific racists to argue that its majority ethnicity was of inferior Mongoloid stock.

question.text: Hone Heke cut down James Busby's flagstaff to start the First Maori War, which is often described with this term. It is also applied to a "Great" conflict fought between Charles XII and Peter the Great.
question.clue: The second conflict of this name saw Azov returned to the Ottoman Turks following their victory at the Battle of Pruth River.

swap.leadin: This ship was salvaged in 1961, over 300 years after sinking on its maiden voyage.
swap.text: Name this ship, now housed at a namesake museum in Stockholm. This ship shares its name with the dynasty of its commissioner, who was advised by Axel Oxenstierna.
swap.clue: A queen from this royal house abdicated after converting to Catholicism and housed Descartes in his final years.

question.leadin: Answer the following about insane CIA Cold War plots that did not involve exploding cigars or acoustic kitties.
question.text: This place was long thought to contain a lost hydrogen bomb after a secret mission crashed at Thule Air Base. Project Iceworm wanted to build launch sites under this territory of Denmark, which is the world's largest island.
question.clue: Henrik Kauffman signed a 1941 treaty with the United States paving the way for the establishment of Thule Airbase on this island.

swap.text: One of the prisoners taken in the Turkish Raid, Guðriður Simonardottir, was later redeemed by this king. This Danish monarch entered his country into the Thirty Years' War, which led his country to call the conflict "The Emperor's War."
swap.clue: He heroically received thirteen wounds onboard the Trinity during the Battle of Kolberge Heath, but persevered to continue fighting the Torstenson War, which his country would eventually lose.

question.leadin: This document was drafted by early New Zealand settler and prominent Darwinian Evolution critic D. G. Monrad.
question.text: Name this progressive document adopted in 1849 to replace the King's Law under pressure from both the National Liberals and Friends of the Peasants. A "November" version of this document created in 1863 sparked an invasion by octogenarian Field Marshall "Papa Wrangel."
question.answerHtml: The Constitution of Denmark [accept First Constitution of Denmark; accept First Danish Constitution; prompt on Constitution or November Constitution by asking “of what country?”]

swap.leadin: The 1917 to '18 dispute over this territory is a textbook example of how the principle of self-determination shapes diplomacy in international law.
swap.text: Name this archipelago in the Baltic Sea that was the subject of a dispute between Sweden and Finland that ended with these islands of Swedes staying Finnish but becoming mostly autonomous.
swap.clue: In the 1920s, the League of Nations notably arbitrated Finland's dispute with Sweden over these islands in the mouth of the Gulf of Bothnia. The League found them to be over 90% Swedish in population, and thus naturally awarded them to Finland.
